bibl.title: Impact of Coordinate Transformation Uncertainty on Human Sensorimotor Control

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: mechanism
span.quote: In summary, we showed that grasping behavior adjusts for coordinate transformation uncertainty introduced by errors in eye position sensing, suggesting the brain has an internal model capable of predicting the consequences of CTU.

span.label: coordinate transformation uncertainty in reach-to-grasp
span.quote: Consequently, target information acquires additional coordinate transformation uncertainty (CTU) during remapping because of errors in joint angle sensing.

span.label: behavioural-experiment
span.quote: To experimentally test for CTU compensation, head-fixed participants repeatedly reached to an occluded cylindrical target while fixating targets that spanned an 80° range of eye positions.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: THE UNCERTAINTY IS MANIPULATED WITHOUT MOVING THE TARGET: the object stays in one place and the participant's EYE POSITION is varied instead, which changes the transformation between eye and head and so adds uncertainty to the remapped location while leaving the object alone
span.quote: To address this question, we varied eye position in the head, while participants reached to grasp a spatially fixed object, both when the object was in view and when it was occluded. Varying eye position changes CTU between eye and head, producing additional uncertainty in remapped information away from forward view.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: THE LEVER IS A KNOWN PROPERTY OF THE SYSTEM RATHER THAN AN INTERVENTION: the authors exploit the fact that error in encoding eye position already varies with saccade magnitude and with eccentricity from forward view, so simply choosing where to look sets the uncertainty
span.quote: To manipulate CTU between the eyes and head, we took advantage of the fact that error in eye position encoding varies both with saccade magnitude and the eye’s eccentricity away from forward view.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: THE PREDICTION IS BUILT AS A CONDITIONAL WITH BOTH ANTECEDENTS NAMED: if the brain stores targets in eye-centred coordinates AND compensates for the effects of the uncertainty, then the grip aperture must vary with eye position EVEN WHEN THE TARGET CANNOT BE SEEN
span.quote: Therefore if the brain stores targets in eye-centered coordinates and compensates for the effects of CTU, it predicts that MGA should also vary as a function of eye position, even when the target is occluded.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the target is deliberately NEVER MOVED across the workspace, and the reason is stated: so that any change in reaching behaviour must come from eye position and viewing eccentricity rather than from the kinematic demands of reaching somewhere else
span.quote: The cylinder was not moved across the workspace to assure that any changes in reaching behavior resulted from changes in eye position/viewing eccentricity and not kinematic demands.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: and its position was CHOSEN to maximise the very quantity under study - placed so that the widest possible range of eye positions away from the target was available, giving the greatest range of uncertainty
span.quote: Moreover, the cylinder’s location was selected such that there was the maximal range of eye positions away from the target (0 – 80°) to allow for the greatest range of uncertainty.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: ONE FIXATION POINT IS DROPPED PURELY TO KEEP THE TWO CONDITIONS COMPARABLE: the zero-degree fixation is excluded because the occluder would block both the target and that fixation letter, so the visual and occluded groups see the same set of fixations
span.quote: The fixation point corresponding to 0° target eccentricity (I) was excluded to keep similar fixations for both the visual and target occluded participants (because the occluder blocks both the target and the 0° fixation letter).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: TWO DESIGNS ARE RUN WITH THE SAME NUMBER OF REPETITIONS PER FIXATION, and the trade-off between them is stated rather than left implicit: the full range captures the functional form of the response profile, the partial range buys statistical power in less time
span.quote: Note that the partial and full range conditions both have the same number of repetitions (147) per fixation point. However, the full range condition allowed us to capture the full functional form of the MGA profile, whereas the partial range condition allowed us to gain statistical power over a shorter period of time.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: visual information is removed at DIFFERENT MOMENTS DURING the reach using liquid crystal shutter glasses, while separate occluders remove information about the hand and the target
span.quote: Occluders were used in the visual and target occluded conditions to remove any information about the hand and target. Moreover, liquid crystal shutter glasses (Milgram 1987) were used to remove visual information at different moments during the reach

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the read-out is justified by prior work before it is used: maximum grip aperture is known to scale with object size and to INCREASE when visual information is degraded
span.quote: Previous work shows that maximum grip aperture scales with object size (Paulignan et al. 1991, 1997) and also increases when visual information is degraded

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the experimental logic is stated as an if-then over that read-out: if grip aperture changes with eye position when the target is OCCLUDED, that is taken to suggest the brain uses knowledge of the transformation uncertainty when planning a reach from a stored location
span.quote: We tested whether reaching behavior similarly adjusts for changes in target location uncertainty introduced by varying CTU. Specifically, participants reached to the remembered locations of occluded targets while eye position was varied. The experimental logic is that if we find that maximum grip aperture changes with eye position when the target is occluded, it suggests the brain uses knowledge of CTU for reach planning that results from remapping stored target location information between eyeand headcentered coordinates.

span.label: An attentional-load account of the occluded-condition effect cannot be excluded by the data, only argued against.
span.note: what this limits: the target-uncertainty account of the occluded condition: IT MAY BE THAT HOLDING EYE POSITION AWAY FROM FORWARD VIEW CREATES AN ATTENTIONAL LOAD THAT AFFECTS GRASPING
span.quote: Although we attribute the change in grasping behavior in the occluded condition to target uncertainty, it may be that holding eye position away from forward view creates an attentional load that affects grasping.

span.label: The results are consistent with, but do not establish exclusive, eye-centred storage; multiple simultaneous reference frames remain possible.
span.note: what this limits: any exclusive claim for eye-centred storage: OUR RESULTS DO NOT PRECLUDE THE POSSIBILITY THAT TARGET INFORMATION IS STORED IN MULTIPLE COORDINATE FRAMES
span.quote: Note that our results do not preclude the possibility that target information is stored in multiple coordinate frames (Avillac 2005).

span.label: The visual fixation marks used in the task may themselves have induced the eye-centred storage strategy the study infers.
span.note: what this limits: the eye-centred conclusion, which the apparatus may have produced: ANOTHER POSSIBILITY IS THAT VISUAL FIXATION MARKS PROMOTED AN EYECENTERED STORAGE STRATEGY
span.quote: Another possibility is that visual fixation marks promoted an eyecentered storage strategy.

span.label: The model assumes large memory uncertainty and the data could not adjudicate a limited-memory alternative.
span.note: what this limits: the large-memory-uncertainty assumption: WE COULD NOT REJECT A LIMITED MEMORY MODEL ON THE BASIS OF CROSS-TRIAL ANALYSES - ANY INFLUENCES OF FIXATIONS FROM PREVIOUS TRIALS WERE TOO SMALL TO BE RELIABLY MEASURED
span.quote: In addition, we could not reject a limited memory model on the basis of cross-trial analyses—any influences of fixations from previous trials were too small to be reliably measured.

span.label: The paper's own alternative explanation is that the apparatus induced the strategy the study infers: the visual fixation marks may have 'promoted an eye-centered storage strategy', being usable to maintain a representation of the body's configuration with respect to the apparatus. It is raised as a possibility and not settled, so the inference from behaviour to storage frame is conditional on the fixation marks not having supplied the frame.
span.quote: Another possibility is that visual fixation marks promoted an eyecentered storage strategy. In particular, fixation marks may have been used to maintain an accurate representation of the body’s configuration with respect to the apparatus.

span.label: a Bayesian model of location inference used to predict how grip aperture compensates for coordinate-transformation uncertainty
span.quote: the amount of compensation is predicted by a Bayesian model for location inference that uses eye-centered storage. information and for changes in CTU when the target INTRODUCTION When humans reach out and grasp an object, information about the object’s location arrives at different times through multiple sensory modalities, each in its own frame of reference.

span.label: the whole experiment was re-run on a DIFFERENT GROUP with a visual occluder that showed the target but not the hand
span.note: eliminates: that maximum grip aperture reflects something other than uncertainty about object LOCATION - the occluder holds target visibility constant while removing hand vision
span.quote: To verify that MGA is a measure of object location uncertainty, we subsequently ran the same experiment on a different group of subjects with a visual occluder that allowed view of the target, but not the hand (Fig.

span.label: a fully visual condition run alongside the uncertainty conditions
span.note: eliminates: that grip aperture fails to track uncertainty at all - the visual condition establishes that the measure responds when it should
span.quote: The visual condition allowed us to verify that MGA is encoding target uncertainty for the task.

span.label: remapping
span.quote: We term the uncertainty about the relationship between body segments caused by imperfect sensory knowledge coordinate transformation uncertainty (CTU; Fig. 1). When there is CTU in a system, estimates are degraded by each transformation made between coordinate frames. Recent work by Sober and Sabes (2005) suggests that people select coordinate representations that minimize the impact of errors caused by remapping.

span.label: reference frame
span.quote: Consequently, target information acquires additional coordinate transformation uncertainty (CTU) during remapping because of errors in joint angle sensing. As a result, CTU creates differences in the reliability of target information depending on the reference frame used for storage.

span.label: fixation marks
span.quote: Another possibility is that visual fixation marks promoted an eyecentered storage strategy. In particular, fixation marks may have been used to maintain an accurate representation of the body’s configuration with respect to the apparatus.

span.label: saccade magnitude → eye position
span.note: THE TWO CANNOT BE SEPARATED IN THIS STUDY - the DESIGN form of the negative relation (Q-286/Q-287). No edge type can express it: all eight assert that a relation HOLDS. A confounding statement bounds what the paper's own results can mean, and it lives where nothing downstream will find it. Two sources of the same uncertainty, inseparable because of where the subjects were asked to look.
span.quote: Because subjects saccade to the (cid:5) wee and (cid:1) (cid:5) we pe pe fixation points from forward view for the experimental data presented here, we cannot distinguish between uncertainty due to saccade magnitude from uncertainty caused by eye position.

span.label: reliability - AS A PROPERTY OF THE STORAGE FORMAT, NOT OF THE MEASUREMENT: the same target information is more or less reliable according to which coordinate frame holds it, because each remapping between frames degrades the estimate
span.quote: Consequently, target information acquires additional coordinate transformation uncertainty (CTU) during remapping because of errors in joint angle sensing. As a result, CTU creates differences in the reliability of target information depending on the reference frame used for storage.

span.label: builds-on → Sober and Sabes (2005)
span.quote: Sober and Sabes (2005) showed that people use knowledge about CTU when integrating current sensory information.

span.label: extends → neural and pointing evidence for eye-centred target storage (Batista et al. 1999; Pouget et al. 2002; Henriques et al. 1998; Crawford et al. 2004; Lewald and Ehrenstein 2000; Mergner et al. 2001)
span.quote: These results extend previous neural (Batista et al. 1999; Pouget et al. 2002) and psychophysical evidence (from pointing) (Crawford et al. 2004; Henriques et al. 1998; Lewald and Ehrenstein 2000; Mergner et al. 2001) for eyecentered target storage by showing that eye-centered storage persists in a task for which there is no visual information specifying target location.

span.label: extends → Lewald and Ehrenstein (2000) pointing data
span.quote: To show the effect of CTU on pointing behavior, we modeled data from a previously published experiment (Lewald and Ehrenstein 2000).

span.label: remapping —causes→ coordinate transformation uncertainty
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.9 — EVERY CONVERSION BETWEEN REPRESENTATIONS COSTS ACCURACY, STATED FLATLY: 'When there is CTU in a system, ESTIMATES ARE DEGRADED BY EACH TRANSFORMATION MADE BETWEEN COORDINATE FRAMES.' And the system is said to respond by choosing its format accordingly - 'people SELECT COORDINATE REPRESENTATIONS THAT MINIMIZE THE IMPACT OF ERRORS caused by remapping' (Sober and Sabes 2005). The format is not a neutral container: it is picked to minimise conversion loss.
span.quote: We term the uncertainty about the relationship between body segments caused by imperfect sensory knowledge coordinate transformation uncertainty (CTU; Fig. 1). When there is CTU in a system, estimates are degraded by each transformation made between coordinate frames. Recent work by Sober and Sabes (2005) suggests that people select coordinate representations that minimize the impact of errors caused by remapping.

span.label: reference frame —causes→ coordinate transformation uncertainty
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.9 — THE SAME TARGET IS MORE OR LESS RELIABLE DEPENDING ON WHICH FRAME IT IS STORED IN: 'CTU creates DIFFERENCES IN THE RELIABILITY of target information DEPENDING ON THE REFERENCE FRAME USED FOR STORAGE.' The reliability is a property of the storage format rather than of the object measured, which is why the paper can infer the frame from behaviour at all.
span.quote: Consequently, target information acquires additional coordinate transformation uncertainty (CTU) during remapping because of errors in joint angle sensing. As a result, CTU creates differences in the reliability of target information depending on the reference frame used for storage.
